headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can leak account/media data into Superset workflows, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict remain limited by missing shared channels and write scopes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A can ingest local media files and account data, but it has no filesystem read/write or MCP surface, so direct injection paths are limited. Profile B only exposes the Superset API and allowlisted egress. Without a documented shared channel, the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies untrusted text from A into B's Superset inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, attacker-controlled content can cross from A to B.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate accounts/sessions.
Disable copy-paste of generated text into Superset.
Use a read-only staging folder for any shared artifacts.
Add provenance labels to imported content.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization before B ingests A outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile A touches video, images, and account data and has broad network egress; profile B has allowlisted egress and a Superset API surface. Even without a shared workspace, any operator-mediated transfer of A's media or account artifacts into B can expose sensitive content in default workflows. The pair is not proven to share storage, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A outputs account-linked media into a shared workspace, B can ingest it.
IF B is configured to publish dashboards or exports containing A-derived artifacts, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Store A outputs in a private folder.
Restrict B to non-sensitive datasets.
Review any dashboard export before sharing.
Rotate any account credentials used by A.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or execute shells, while B only advertises allowlisted network egress. That makes direct write-write contention unlikely. The main conflict is operational overlap on shared external services, but the profiles do not show overlapping mutable scopes, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external dataset or API token, conflicting updates can occur.
IF an orchestrator later grants B filesystem write access, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same dataset.
Schedule runs sequentially.
Lock shared resources during updates.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces upload-oriented outputs from media/account data, and B exposes a Superset API that could render or operationalize imported results. If B treats A's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. Because no direct automation chain is documented, this is inferred rather than observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated metadata without validation, incorrect facts propagate.
IF A's outputs are used as source data for dashboards or alerts, downstream decisions can be wrong.
mitigations: Validate A outputs before import.
Require human review for any A-derived dataset.
Compare A outputs against source records.
Mark imported fields as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance checks in B.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles account data and media uploads, while B's profile shows no special regulated data classes or residency constraints. The pair does not document a specific residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy alignment. I do not cite B's empty data-class list as a violation; it simply means no special compliance surface is declared.
conditions: IF A is used with regulated media or account data, local policy review is needed.
IF B is later connected to regulated datasets, residency and retention rules must be rechecked.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before use.
Avoid regulated data in A outputs.
Set retention limits on exported artifacts.
Document who can access shared reports.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
